messages:
hao: quick heads-up 1 i'm drafting a very small "provisioning quick checks" doc for Dedicated capacity. A one-pager: pre-provision checklist, common failures, autoscale mapping, and three tiny snippets (CLI, terraform migration hint, Ruby SDK).

rebekah: love the scope. can you call out the most common failure we see: tenant label mismatch vs org name? customers hit silent autoscale fallbacks.

hao: yes. adding a 2-line check: `rwdctl tenant validate-labels --tenant T-321` and a note about label normalization.

omar: tiny nit 1 include a grep/CI hook example so infra teams fail fast on legacy scale keys. people run terraform apply and then panic.

hao: good idea. adding CI snippet: 
```sh
# CI pre-apply check (bash)
if grep -R "scale_policy:\s*legacy" --quiet; then
  echo "ERROR: legacy scale_policy found. Run tf-migrate-autoscale or update to balanced/throughput/cost_saver"
  exit 1
fi
```

jas: for the autoscale mapping please include an explicit mapping line (short): legacy -> balanced, legacy_high -> throughput, legacy_saver -> cost_saver. Customers keep asking exact mappings.

hao: added mapping and a one-sentence heuristic: "prefer throughput for steady high QPS, balanced for mixed workloads, cost_saver when unit cost matters."

rebekah: also show a terraform hint so people can copy/paste to migrate. keep it pseudo but runnable.

hao: terraform migration hint: 
```hcl
# migration hint: convert old legacy enums to new values
resource "rwd_dedicated_pool" "p" {
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  autoscale {
    policy = "balanced" # map legacy -> balanced/throughput/cost_saver as appropriate
  }
}
```

omar: add a CLI dry-run example. we see accidental commits when ppl skip --dry-run. show both preview and commit.

hao: CLI examples: 
```bash
# preview reserved pool creation
rwdctl reserved create --tenant T-321 --gpu a100-80gb --region us-east-1 --dry-run
# commit when ready
rwdctl reserved create --tenant T-321 --gpu a100-80gb --region us-east-1 --commit
```

jas: troubleshooting bullets please: certs for private deploy, quota exceeded, kms permission denied, terraform validation errors. one-liners ok.

hao: adding 4-step triage: 1) validate labels, 2) check region quotas (`aws service-quotas`), 3) verify KMS key policy/principal, 4) check provisioner logs (`rwdctl logs provisioner --tenant T-321 --since 30m`).

rebekah: BIG ask 1 call out isolation decorator behavior very clearly. If a decorator moves a tenant to reserved routing their SLA/latency profile can change. Add a short note to contact CSM.

hao: will add a short warning: "Isolation annotations may route traffic to reserved capacity and change latency SLOs; confirm SLA deltas with your CSM before enabling in prod." Also include small yaml example: 
```yaml
# isolation annotation example
annotations:
  rwd.io/isolation: "reserved"
  rwd.io/priority: "latency-1"
```

omar: one more unique snippet request 1 can we add a tiny Ruby SDK example showing how to request a dedicated model variant at request-time? that one is surprisingly common in support tickets.

hao: draft Ruby snippet: 
```ruby
# ruby snippet: prefer dedicated route
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['RWD_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(
  model: 'redwood-dedicated/gpt-3-dedicated-v1',
  input: 'hello',
  routing: { 'tier' => 'dedicated' }
)
puts resp.output
```

jas: link fix: docs currently point to internal quota spreadsheet. replace with `/docs/dedicated/quota-matrix` and add "(internal breakdown available to partners)" footnote.

hao: done. also adding a small "what breaks" section with 3 bullets: terraform silent reject, API validation errors, and unexpected cost/throughput mismatch when choosing wrong policy.

build-bot: PR opened by hao: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/docs/+/7890 :eyes:

rebekah: i will review the PR tonight. main things to check: CI grep, mapping table wording, and the Ruby snippet formatting. keep the page <1 screen if possible.

hao: thanks 1 aiming to merge after one technical review and a quick linter pass. will ping when live on the site. :shipit:
